# Get started

Topographer requires Python 3.11 or newer. Install it from GitHub:

```bash
pip install "topographer[plotting] @ git+https://github.com/oist/topographer.git"
```

With uv, use `uv add "topographer[plotting] @ git+https://github.com/oist/topographer.git"`.
The `plotting` extra provides the dependencies for charts; omit it if you do
not need plots. Contributors building the site can install the `docs` extra.

## A small scalar network

Give each vertex an ID and a scalar value, then construct a topology workspace.
The join and split trees summarize sublevel and superlevel connectivity.

```python
import rustworkx as rx
from topographer import Graph, ScalarNetwork, ScalarNetworkTopology
from topographer.plotting import build_tree_plot_data, plot_tree

backend = rx.PyGraph()
backend.add_nodes_from([
    {"id": "a", "height": 0.0},
    {"id": "b", "height": 1.0},
    {"id": "c", "height": 0.3},
])
backend.add_edges_from([(0, 1, None), (1, 2, None)])
graph = Graph.from_rustworkx(backend, vertex_id_attr="id", vertex_attribute_cols=("height",))
network = ScalarNetwork(graph, scalar_attr="height")
topology = ScalarNetworkTopology(network)
join_tree = topology.compute_merge_tree("sublevel")
split_tree = topology.compute_merge_tree("superlevel")
pairs = join_tree.persistence()
diagram = topology.persistence_diagram("sublevel")
simplified = join_tree.simplify(persistence_threshold=0.2)
chart = plot_tree(build_tree_plot_data(simplified, root_kind="maximum"))
```

Display `chart` in a notebook to explore the result. See the [Gallery](../gallery/index.qmd)
for complete examples and the [User guide](../guide/index.qmd) for more workflows.
